articles.title: Nifty target at 26,200 as BofA tweaks India strategy; upgrades hospitals, telecom, downgrades two-wheelers
articles.excerpt:
Bank of America (BofA) Securities has retained its year-end Nifty target of 26,200, indicating a further upside potential of 4.7% from current levels, as it sees India's equity market risks gradually receding and corporate earnings showing signs of recovery.

In its latest India strategy report, the brokerage said most of the major uncertainties that had weighed on markets are now better understood and largely factored into valuations. These include elevated crude oil and commodity prices, a weaker monsoon, rupee depreciation, potential interest rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve and the Reserve Bank of India, and large fundraising activity.

articles.title: Financial stocks hold Nifty steady at midday; Auto, FMCG drag
articles.excerpt:
Benchmark indices were nearly flat at midday on Thursday, with financial stocks providing support even as automobiles and consumer goods weighed on sentiment. The BSE Sensex was trading at 81,930.41, up 51.01 points or 0.06 per cent, while the NSE Nifty 50 was at 25,255.55, up just 0.50 points or 0.00 per cent, as of 12.50 pm, marking the first session since October 9 where the index stayed within the range of the previous bar.

articles.title: Sterling drops against firmer dollar as markets price in a hawkish Fed
articles.excerpt:
The pound fell against the dollar following strong US inflation data and comments from Federal Reserve officials. Despite recent hawkish expectations supporting the pound, crude oil prices are rising, which could be unfavorable. Britain's gross domestic product data is due soon, with growth expectations for the third quarter. Analysts remain skeptical about the Bank of England achieving inflation targets before 2030.
